name: r2-revise-1
statement: The accuracy-carrying part of the Olmo-3.1 RL-Zero-Math delta is its dense sign pattern over many small entries, which moves logits to first order as a coherent sum with high Fisher leverage per unit norm; magnitudes, the most-changed entries and the low-rank head (top singular directions) carry only their proportional share of it, so an arm recovers accuracy in proportion to how much of the coherent sign pattern it keeps in expectation (per-problem log-odds roughly linear in that share), DARE survives until its scaled noise breaks the network, sign randomization gives nothing, and the Code-RL pattern, which agrees with Math-RL in sign at chance, gives no math gain.
scope: Olmo-3-1025-7B base vs Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math (step 2,800) and Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Code, all 2-D weight matrices, partial copies, truncations, sign edits and doses of the delta; MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 (n13 setting) and T 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3. Does not cover SFT deltas beyond explaining why DARE fails on them, the cue, or sampling-only results. Forced by: 2511.08567 (restricting an RLVR update to principal directions is worst) and 2610.37719 (effect sits in signs, c_sign/c_profile about 1; sign-flip null loses it), which contradict the parent r1-surprises-2's claim that a few singular directions carry the function; and result-c9b27e's chance sign agreement, which contradicts r1-all-2's claim that Code-RL shares the switch.

explains.quote: random neurons matched on change energy (two kinds) 58.0-63.8: H_local REFUTED
explains.how: Ranking neurons by change magnitude finds nothing because the effect sits in the signs, not in large entries: the top set holds only its share of the sign pattern.

explains.quote: while carrying 33-1,000x the change energy: H_diffuse SUPPORTED
explains.how: DARE keeps every entry's sign in expectation, so the coherent sum survives while the rescaled noise adds no systematic push.

explains.quote: yet it scores like the whole MLP delta
explains.how: With high sign coherence the DARE damage term (1-p)/(p*rho_sign) of 2610.37719 stays small down to q = 0.1 %, so 33-1,000x the change energy costs almost nothing.
An SFT delta has low sign coherence (published rho_sign below 6) and large entries, so the same sparse copy is dominated by noise and fails.

explains.quote: the imitation delta (24.8% of norm, 100x larger) does not point along RL
explains.how: The SFT delta is a different kind of update (large, low coherence), consistent with DARE failing on SFT and working on RL.

explains.quote: 88 % of all 352,256 neurons have a positive score
explains.how: A dense sign pattern gives almost every neuron a small positive share of the effect.
A coherent first-order sum over entries adds linearly, as the summed scores (0.542 vs 0.549 nats) show.
A random subset closes about its proportional share of the KL, as expected if function is spread evenly over the sign pattern.
Math-RL and Code-RL share the updated-entry mask (set by the base, 2511.08567) but not the signs, so they carry different functions.
A small dense shift acts only where it aligns with high-Fisher directions, which math solutions engage and general text does not.

conflicts.quote: 11.8% of its squared norm sits in 8 singular directions per matrix
conflicts.how: The delta has a low-rank head 15-20x above null with deliberation-word readouts; the theory says it carries only its 12 % share of function, and does not explain why RL wrote such a head.

conflicts.quote: Every arm that recovers accuracy also takes RL's format and length
conflicts.how: The theory predicts that a small dose flips the 'Answer:' format (a large per-token log-ratio) without the accuracy; the n13 arms never separated the two, so this is untested, but it reads against the theory.

conflicts.quote: on a cap-limited model a random edit of matched norm can give most of an accuracy gain
conflicts.how: On a 0.8B model with 95 % cap hits a random edit helped; the theory predicts a sign-randomized delta gives the base nothing. Scope difference (Olmo plain base caps far less), but a real tension.

conflicts.quote: MLP layers 0-15 carry about twice what 16-31 do
conflicts.how: A function spread evenly over the sign pattern does not predict a 2:1 layer asymmetry; it needs early-layer Fisher to be higher.

rival: r1-surprises-2: the function lives in a few coherent singular directions per matrix and the high-rank remainder is noise. Separation: rank-8 truncation of each matrix's delta vs the delta minus its rank-8 truncation. The rival predicts about 435 and 340 right of 500 (T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, plain); this theory predicts about 335 and 455. A second separator against r1-all-2 (redundant switch): r1-all-2 predicts DARE at q = 0.01 % still works and base + 0.25*(RL - base) plain at T 1.0 reaches about 375; this theory predicts collapse and about 308.

imports.finding: For Olmo-3-7B RL-Zero deltas the Fisher leverage of the RL direction is about 700x a random same-norm direction, the effect sits in signs and cross-coordinate structure (magnitude alignment about 1), a sign-flip null loses it, and DARE damage follows (1-p)/(p*rho_sign).
imports.how: Turns 'DARE works, top-k fails' into a quantitative rule: accuracy follows the kept sign pattern, noise damage scales as 1/(p*rho), so DARE must break below some keep rate (predicted collapse at q = 0.01 %, where per-matrix noise reaches about 24 % of weight norm), and a sign-flipped delta of equal magnitudes gives near-base accuracy.

imports.finding: RLVR updates avoid principal directions; restricting an update to principal weights tracks dense RLVR worst, and RL runs from one base share the updated-entry mask while their directions differ.
imports.how: Predicts that the delta's top singular directions are not where accuracy lives (rank-8 truncation near base, its complement near RL), and explains the 1.64x shared mask with chance sign agreement between Math-RL and Code-RL, so Code-RL gives no math gain.

imports.finding: Two independent RL updates from one base have cosine 0.003-0.037 (data sets the direction), and the math gain is redundant across large components of the update (off-diagonal-only 74 %, null-space-only 80 %).
imports.how: Makes the team's cos 0.014 the normal level for unrelated RL runs rather than evidence of a shared switch, and supports that any large complement of a small subset (the delta minus its rank-8 part) keeps most of the gain.

predictions.experiment: Base + rank-8 SVD truncation of (RL - base) in every 2-D matrix, plain prompt in chat template, MATH-500 n=500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, grader v3, one sample (v3 endpoints: base 305-319, RL 464)
predictions.refuted_by: 400 or more right (the low-rank head carries the gain)

predictions.experiment: Base + (delta minus its rank-8 truncation) in every 2-D matrix, same setting; also share of answers with an 'Answer:' line
predictions.refuted_by: fewer than 415 right, or an 'Answer:' line in more than 15 % of answers (the remainder would lack RL's format)

predictions.experiment: Base + sign-flipped delta: every changed entry keeps its |delta| but gets a random sign (seed 0), unchanged entries stay 0, plain prompt, MATH-500 n=500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, grader v3
predictions.refuted_by: 345 or more right (a directionless edit of the delta's magnitudes gives a gain)

predictions.experiment: DARE on the MLP delta at keep q = 0.01 % (each entry kept with probability 1e-4, scaled by 10,000; attention and norms base), plain prompt, MATH-500 n=500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, grader v3
predictions.refuted_by: 300 or more right (the DARE plateau extends to q = 0.01 %)

predictions.experiment: Base + 0.25*(RL - base), plain prompt, MATH-500 n=500, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, one sample (endpoints plain base 224, RL 463); the 'Answer:' line share is expected to fall below 15 % even though accuracy stays low
predictions.refuted_by: 370 or more right (a concave, switch-like dose)

predictions.experiment: Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Code final checkpoint (= base + Code-RL delta), plain prompt, MATH-500 n=500, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, one sample
predictions.refuted_by: 320 or more right (Code-RL carries part of the math gain)
